labels.name: 0.kind: bug

items.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

I am attempting to add a patch to `pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix` and do not yet know its hash (well, let's pretend).  So I go add the `fetchurl` invocation to the list of patches and set `hash = lib.fakeHash`.  So far, so good.  I am also doing this in a (thus far unsuccessful, but that's beside the point) attempt to get a cross-compilation shell environment for `arm-embedded`.  Unfortunately, the combination of the patched `nixpkgs`, the `nix-2.31.3` interpreter, and an attempt to evaluate `pkgs.pkgsCross.arm-embedded.newlib-nano` results in the world going pear shaped:
```
       error: infinite recursion encountered
       at /dozer/nwf/src/nixos/nixpkgs/pkgs/build-support/fetchurl/default.nix:318:12:
          317|         then
          318|           "${cacert}/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt"
             |            ^
          319|         else
```

### Steps to reproduce

Patch `master` thus:
```diff
diff --git a/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix b/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix
index c7b3ccbe8a85..06bf24329751 100644
--- a/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix
+++ b/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix
@@ -31,6 +31,11 @@ stdenvNoLibc.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
       url = "https://sourceware.org/git/?p=newlib-cygwin.git;a=patch;h=351842d55ee50fab672818b72f2c6bf3be1772bd;hp=4a1144dc540423b422dbec27eb433bc7dc725ae8";
       hash = "sha256-GMx9nQKJEnXbA5HFczp3xjrrU94j1oXq4lIjEf0um9Y=";
     })
+    (fetchpatch {
+      name = "0003-newlib-fix-porting-texi.patch";
+      url = "https://sourceware.org/git/?p=newlib-cygwin.git;a=patch;h=f43cd384d0f124e51de86374bd97ce08d6fdc82e";
+      hash = lib.fakeHash;
+    })
   ]
   ++ lib.optionals nanoizeNewlib [
     # https://bugs.gentoo.org/723756
```
And then attempt to evaluate...
| → with ↓                  | `pkgs.newlib-nano` | `pkgs.pkgsCross.arm-embedded.newlib-nano` |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `lix-2.96.0-pre-20260317` | OK                 | OK                                        |
| `nix-2.31.3`              | OK                 | infinite recursion                        |

### Expected behaviour

Successful evaluation?  Lack of divergence on `nix`-the-language semantics between cppnix and lix?

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console

```

### Additional context

To work around this issue, it suffices to supply basically any other hash (correct or not!) in the patch above, because https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/eb22156503b59b106d3792a7bd7d006c85b005ac/pkgs/build-support/fetchurl/default.nix#L308-L320 is looking specifically for some particular fake ones.  In particular, supplying the correct hash, thus, will result in derivations completing successfully.
```
diff --git a/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix b/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix
index c7b3ccbe8a85..f722d6678296 100644
--- a/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix
+++ b/pkgs/by-name/ne/newlib/package.nix
@@ -31,6 +31,11 @@ stdenvNoLibc.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {
       url = "https://sourceware.org/git/?p=newlib-cygwin.git;a=patch;h=351842d55ee50fab672818b72f2c6bf3be1772bd;hp=4a1144dc540423b422dbec27eb433bc7dc725ae8";
       hash = "sha256-GMx9nQKJEnXbA5HFczp3xjrrU94j1oXq4lIjEf0um9Y=";
     })
+    (fetchpatch {
+      name = "0003-newlib-fix-porting-texi.patch";
+      url = "https://sourceware.org/git/?p=newlib-cygwin.git;a=patch;h=f43cd384d0f124e51de86374bd97ce08d6fdc82e";
+      hash = "sha256-02VooJZLm38eSG7rDoMsRe/gll+5lyh03Hs3VKuGhSo=";
+    })
   ]
   ++ lib.optionals nanoizeNewlib [
     # https://bugs.gentoo.org/723756
```

-----

This issue is sort of related to #428266, in that overriding the `cacert` parameter to `fetchurl` thusly will result in `nix-2.31.3` also evaluating `pkgs.pkgsCross.arm-embedded.newlib-nano` successfully:
```
diff --git a/pkgs/top-level/all-packages.nix b/pkgs/top-level/all-packages.nix
index 2b9c723ffd38..6c652ec68cc9 100644
--- a/pkgs/top-level/all-packages.nix
+++ b/pkgs/top-level/all-packages.nix
@@ -590,7 +590,7 @@ with pkgs;
     else
       makeOverridable (import ../build-support/fetchurl) {
         inherit lib stdenvNoCC buildPackages;
-        inherit cacert;
+        inherit (buildPackages) cacert;
         inherit (config) hashedMirrors rewriteURL;
         curl = buildPackages.curlMinimal.override (old: rec {
           # break dependency cycles
```

I sort of think that `lix` is right, here, in that the above patch is modifying the `else` branch of https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/eb22156503b59b106d3792a7bd7d006c85b005ac/pkgs/top-level/all-packages.nix#L586-L594, in which `stdenv.buildPlatform == stdenv.hostPlatform`, and so I expect the `inherit` to operate in a world where `buildPackages` _is_ `hostPackages` and _is_ the package set currently being defined, but perhaps I am missing something about how all this splicing works.

items.body:
### Describe the bug
When using `~/.config/nixpkgs/config.nix` to configure nixpkgs, this file may optionally be a function that takes a single `{ pkgs }:` parameter. This is necessary when adding configuration for `blocklistedLicenses` in order to reference the licenses in question. Example usage:

```nix
{ pkgs }:

{
  blocklistedLicenses = with pkgs.lib.licenses; [ agpl3Only agpl3Plus ];
}
```

As of https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/240433 (darwin.stdenv: Darwin stdenv rework), the reference to `pkgs` within this file produces an infinite recursion error:

```
error:
       … <borked>

         at «none»:0: (source not available)

       … while evaluating a branch condition

         at /Users/lily/Dev/Nix/nixpkgs/pkgs/stdenv/booter.nix:99:7:

           98|     thisStage =
           99|       if args.__raw or false
             |       ^
          100|       then args'

       (stack trace truncated; use '--show-trace' to show the full trace)

       error: infinite recursion encountered

       at /Users/lily/.config/nixpkgs/config.nix:4:30:

            3| {
            4|   blocklistedLicenses = with pkgs.lib.licenses; [ agpl3Only agpl3Plus ];
             |                              ^
            5| }
```

### Steps To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Ensure your nixpkgs contains commit a845397040d1b85cec4ee41edb8598d8086c3d95
2. Ensure the file `~/.config/nixpkgs/config.nix` contains the contents listed above and that there is no `NIXPKGS_CONFIG` env var (or set `NIXPKGS_CONFIG` to the path of a file containing the above)
3. Run something like `nix-instantiate --eval --expr 'with import ./. {}; hello.version'` (if from a nixpkgs checkout, or import `<nixpkgs>` if appropriate).

### Expected behavior
This should run successfully (in this case, printing the version of the `hello` package).

### Additional context
Merely doing something like `blocklistedLicenses = assert builtins.isAttrs pkgs; [];` is sufficient to cause this issue. Sticking this in some of the other config values (like `allowUnfree`) doesn't cause a problem, though I didn't test all of them. Looking at the full stack trace I think it's because it's trying to test the validity of `../../build-support/cc-wrapper` during bootstrap, so it's likely just the allowlisted/blocklisted licenses that will end up evaluated here.

I really wish the config here was given `{ lib }` instead, but that's a backwards-incompatible change.

Folks involved in the relevant PR: @reckenrode @viraptor @veprbl @emilazy @Atemu @tjni @willcohen @siraben @uri-canva

items.body:
Apologies for the combined PR. They intersect at `checkConfigNotError`. Can split if desired nonetheless.

This adds two new error contexts, and a little addition to the test runner.

# Loading imports of module

```
       … while loading imports of module `/home/user/nixpkgs/lib/tests/modules/import-configuration.nix`
```

- only for the latest ok-ish module, not the whole chain
- see commit message

# Infinite recursion through module argument

```
       … while calling 'config''
         at /home/user/h/nixpkgs/lib/modules.nix:509:9:
          508|       config' =
          509|         name:
             |         ^
          510|           builtins.addErrorContext

       … *risky* while evaluating the module fixpoint, `config`

       Note that the module structure and `imports` fundamentally can not depend on the module fixpoint!
       An argument `someUnknownArg` was not provided externally through .specialArgs., so we try to load it from the module fixpoint...
       If the following message is "infinite recursion", this was the cause, and possible solutions include:
       - Perhaps someUnknownArg was misspelled.
       - Make sure that the module was loaded into the right context.
       - Provide the argument externally through `specialArgs`.
       - Structure the module such that the top level attribute set and special attributes like `config`, `imports` and `config._module.args` do not refer to `someUnknownArg`.
         (Except perhaps in a deeper structure, like a more deeply nested attribute, or a `mkIf` condition.)

       The above explanation is new. If it is inaccurate or out of place, please report a minimal example in a Nixpkgs issue and ping the Module System maintainers.


       error: infinite recursion encountered
```

for an example like

```nix
let
  b =
    { someUnknownArg, ... }: {
      imports = [ someUnknownArg ];
    };
in
{
  _file = "a";
  imports = [ b ];
```

items.title: check-meta: infinite recursion when Nixpkgs `config` is a function of `pkgs` (aarch64-darwin)
items.body:
### Nixpkgs version

`master` at `c89bab9ae1dc` (also reproduced at `0fd946d51539` and `38bba8d156fd`).

### Describe the bug

Evaluating Nixpkgs with `config` defined as a **function of `pkgs`** fails with `error: infinite recursion encountered` on `aarch64-darwin`. That is the form `pkgs/test/config-nix-unit.nix` covers in `testStandaloneConfigFunctionPkgs`, so `tests.config-nix-unit` fails there (7/8) while passing on Linux.

It surfaces as a red `nixpkgs-review` on unrelated pull requests, since `config-nix-unit` lands in almost every impacted set.

### Steps to reproduce

It is an *evaluation* failure, so it reproduces from any platform by setting `system`:

```console
$ nix-instantiate --eval --strict --expr '(import <nixpkgs> {
    system = "aarch64-darwin";
    config = { pkgs, lib, ... }: { allowUnfree = lib.isAttrs pkgs; };
  }).config.allowUnfree'
error: infinite recursion encountered
```

|                           | `x86_64-linux` | `aarch64-darwin`   |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------ |
| `master` (`c89bab9ae1dc`) | `true`         | infinite recursion |
| `270c9c9792ee^`           | `true`         | `true`             |

### Expected behaviour

`true`, as on `x86_64-linux` and as `testStandaloneConfigFunctionPkgs` asserts.

### Relevant log output

```
… pkgs/stdenv/generic/make-derivation.nix:983
… pkgs/stdenv/generic/check-meta.nix:472
… pkgs/stdenv/generic/check-meta.nix:177   if allowUnfree then
… pkgs/stdenv/generic/check-meta.nix:73    allowUnfree = config.allowUnfree || …
… while evaluating the option `allowUnfree':
… while evaluating definitions from `nixpkgs.config':
… while evaluating a branch condition at pkgs/stdenv/booter.nix:107:9
error: infinite recursion encountered
```

### Additional context

Bisected across `e701ff054bbf..38bba8d156fd` (1537 commits, 10 steps, no skips) to **270c9c9792ee**, "check-meta: cache allowUnfree", from #548898:

```diff
-    attrs: hasUnfreeLicense attrs && !allowUnfree && !allowUnfreePredicate attrs;
+    if allowUnfree then _: false else attrs: hasUnfreeLicense attrs && !allowUnfreePredicate attrs;
```

The difference is short-circuiting rather than caching. The original tests `hasUnfreeLicense attrs` first, so for a **free** package `&&` short-circuits and `allowUnfree` is never forced — and every package consulted during stdenv bootstrap is free. The new form reads `allowUnfree` up front for every package, so `config` is always forced, which is a cycle when `config` is itself a function of `pkgs`.

Confirmed causal: at `270c9c9792ee`, restoring only `pkgs/stdenv/generic/check-meta.nix` from its parent makes the expression above evaluate `true` again.

@llakala — no criticism intended, the caching in #548898 is a good change and this is an easy strictness edge to miss; flagging it because you have the most context on that series. A few of its other commits hoist conditions the same way, so they may be worth a second look for the same pattern.

I have a fix that keeps the predicate caching while restoring the short-circuit, and will open it shortly.

### System metadata

Evaluated from `x86_64-linux` with `system = "aarch64-darwin"`; the failure is in evaluation, not in a builder.

### Notify maintainers

@llakala

### I assert that this issue is relevant for Nixpkgs

- [X] I assert that this is a bug and not a support request.
- [X] I assert that this is not a duplicate of an existing issue.
- [X] I assert that I have read the NixOS Code of Conduct and agree to abide by it.
